# Qualixar Jev Decision Layer

> One decision runtime with host adapters for Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, Hermes and VS Code. Bounded typed Jev decisions for AI assistants, with an optional local Laya route. Answers are gated locally and never grant tool authority.

Release 1.0.13 is supported and verified on macOS, with hosted TypeSafe Jev and OpenRouter keys in the macOS Keychain. Linux is experimental and unverified. Windows is disabled: its runtime entry points refuse to start because the native private-state contract did not pass CI. Local Laya needs an Apple-Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later and a one-time `jev laya-install`. Jev + Laya decides requests marked `restricted` on the Mac and sends the rest to Jev. Python 3.11 or newer is required. claude.ai in a web browser is not supported. This index is a reading convenience for agents, not a guarantee of search ranking or universal host support. Every claim about a specific harness is qualified in the host guide by what was actually run.

Release 1.0.13 contains 55 recipes and 165 synthetic offline fixtures. To evaluate it without a key, provider call or enrolled workspace, run `plugins/qualixar-jev-decision-layer/scripts/jev selftest`: it replays the fixture set through the real gate offline. A passing run is a contract check on the shipped gate, never evidence of provider accuracy.
